```plato

    //==
    // IReal

    // The absolute value of x (its magnitude on the number line).
    Abs(x: IReal): IReal
        => x.LessThan(x.Zero) ? x.Negative : x;

    // The sign of x as an integer: -1, 0, or +1.
    Sign(x: IReal): Integer
        => x.Compare(x.Zero);

    // The complement of x within the unit interval: one minus x. Handy for weights
    // and easing (e.g. the (1 - t) factor in a Bezier blend).
    OneMinus(x: IReal): IReal
        => x.One - x;

    // True when x is strictly greater than zero.
    IsPositive(x: IReal): Boolean
        => x.Zero.LessThan(x);

    // True when x is strictly less than zero.
    IsNegative(x: IReal): Boolean
        => x.LessThan(x.Zero);

    // True when x and y differ by no more than the given (non-negative) tolerance.
    AlmostEqual(x: IReal, y: IReal, tolerance: IReal): Boolean
        => (x - y).Abs <= tolerance;

    // True when x and y are close under the combined absolute+relative policy:
    // |x - y| <= tol.Absolute + tol.Relative * max(|x|, |y|). This is the library's
    // one numerical-comparison epsilon (see CONVENTIONS.md - Floating-point
    // comparison). Note: engineering Tolerance (uncertainty.types.plato) is an acceptance
    // allowance, NOT ComparisonTolerance, and does not belong here.
    AlmostEqual(x: Number, y: Number, tol: ComparisonTolerance): Boolean
        => (x - y).Abs <= tol.Absolute + tol.Relative * x.Abs.Greater(y.Abs);

    // True when x is within the given (non-negative) tolerance of zero.
    AlmostZero(x: IReal, tolerance: IReal): Boolean
        => x.Abs <= tolerance;

    // True when x sits at either end of the unit interval, within the given
    // (non-negative) tolerance. Useful for detecting degenerate curve parameters.
    AlmostZeroOrOne(x: IReal, tolerance: IReal): Boolean
        => x.AlmostZero(tolerance) || x.AlmostEqual(x.One, tolerance);

    // Clamps x to the inclusive range [0, 1].
    Saturate(x: IReal): IReal
        => x.Clamp(x.Zero, x.One);

    // The parameter t in [0,1] for which Lerp(a, b, t) equals value. Assumes a != b.
    InverseLerp(a: IReal, b: IReal, value: IReal): Number
        => ((value - a) / (b - a)).ToNumber;

    // Remaps value from the input range [inputMin, inputMax] onto the output range
    // [outputMin, outputMax]. Assumes inputMin != inputMax.
    Remap(value: IReal, inputMin: IReal, inputMax: IReal, outputMin: IReal, outputMax: IReal): IReal
        => outputMin.Lerp(outputMax, inputMin.InverseLerp(inputMax, value));

    // Divides x by divisor, returning fallback instead when divisor is zero.
    SafeDivide(x: IReal, divisor: IReal, fallback: IReal): IReal
        => divisor.IsZero ? fallback : x / divisor;

    // The fractional part of x: x minus its floor, always in [0, 1). For negative
    // x this is the periodic fraction (e.g. FractionalPart(-0.25) = 0.75), matching Floor.
    FractionalPart(x: IReal): IReal
        => x - x.Floor;

    // x rounded to the nearest whole value, halves rounding up (toward +infinity),
    // via Floor(x + 1/2). Note: deliberately half-up, unlike the host intrinsic
    // Round (typically banker's rounding) — do not "simplify" to Round.
    RoundedToNearest(x: IReal): IReal
        => (x + x.One.Half).Floor;

    //==
    // Number
    //
    // A small set of shaping helpers that are deliberately Number-concrete rather
    // than generic over Real: they read the `Pow` intrinsic (declared only on
    // Number), and on a type that is simultaneously IMultiplicative and IScalable a
    // generic `x * 2.0` has two equally good readings. IVector/quantity versions
    // belong with the component-wise lifting on `IVector` (P3), not here.

    // x raised to the reciprocal power: the y-th root of x. InversePow(x, 2) is
    // the square root, InversePow(x, 3) the cube root. Precondition: y is not zero.
    InversePow(x: Number, y: Number): Number
        => x.Pow(1.0 / y);

    // The classic smoothstep shaping function 3x^2 - 2x^3, with zero slope at
    // both ends of the unit interval. Assumes x is in [0, 1]; saturate first if not.
    // (For interpolation between two values use SmoothLerp above.)
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoothstep)
    SmoothStep(x: Number): Number
        => x * x * (3.0 - 2.0 * x);

    // Ken Perlin's quintic shaping function 6x^5 - 15x^4 + 10x^3, with zero first
    // AND second derivative at both ends. Assumes x is in [0, 1].
    // Same article family: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoothstep
    SmootherStep(x: Number): Number
        => x * x * x * (x * (x * 6.0 - 15.0) + 10.0);

    // The staircase function: x quantized down to the nearest of `steps` equal
    // treads per unit. Precondition: steps is positive.
    // https://mathworld.wolfram.com/StaircaseFunction.html
    StaircaseFloor(x: Number, steps: Integer): Number
        => (x * steps.ToNumber).Floor / steps.ToNumber;

    // The staircase function quantizing up to the nearest tread of `steps` per
    // unit. Precondition: steps is positive.
    StaircaseCeiling(x: Number, steps: Integer): Number
        => (x * steps.ToNumber).Ceiling / steps.ToNumber;

    // The staircase function quantizing to the nearest tread of `steps` per unit,
    // halves going up. Precondition: steps is positive.
    StaircaseRound(x: Number, steps: Integer): Number
        => (x * steps.ToNumber).RoundedToNearest / steps.ToNumber;

    //==
    // IWhole

    // True when x equals zero.
    IsZero(x: IWhole): Boolean
        => x == x.Zero;

    // True when x equals one.
    IsOne(x: IWhole): Boolean
        => x == x.One;

    // The absolute value of x.
    Abs(x: IWhole): IWhole
        => x.LessThan(x.Zero) ? x.Negative : x;

    // The sign of x as an integer: -1, 0, or +1.
    Sign(x: IWhole): Integer
        => x.Compare(x.Zero);

    // True when x is evenly divisible by two.
    IsEven(x: IWhole): Boolean
        => x.Modulo(x.One + x.One) == x.Zero;

    // True when x is not evenly divisible by two.
    IsOdd(x: IWhole): Boolean
        => x.IsEven.Not;

    // True when x is strictly greater than zero.
    IsPositive(x: IWhole): Boolean
        => x.Zero.LessThan(x);

    // True when x is strictly less than zero.
    IsNegative(x: IWhole): Boolean
        => x.LessThan(x.Zero);
```
